root_cause: Text.append_tokens appended raw token strings without calling strip_control_codes, unlike Text.__init__ and Text.append, which both strip them. A control code such as '\r' stayed in _text, so during wrap the line offsets computed by divide() disagreed with span positions, and divide() indexed line_ranges out of range (IndexError at text.py 'line_start, line_end = line_ranges[end_line_no]').
best_solution: In rich/text.py Text.append_tokens, inside the `for content, style in tokens:` loop, add `content = strip_control_codes(content)` before `append_text(content)`, so the span offsets use the stripped length. strip_control_codes is already imported in text.py. How to get there from the statement: 'exception in append_tokens' plus issue #3014 ('append_tokens does not strip control codes', IndexError when printing a wrapped red token containing '\r\n'). Even without the issue text, comparing append_tokens with its sibling append() shows the one sanitisation step it skips.
acceptable_alternatives: Any change that strips control codes from each token's content before its length is used for the span offset, e.g. building the stripped string once and using it for both append_text and len(). Stripping after the loop, or only in wrap/divide, would leave the spans misaligned or change other outputs.

locating_signals: The statement names the function append_tokens (title 'Fixed exception in append_tokens'), so locating it is trivial. What kind of exception, and what triggers it, is only in the linked issue #3014 (control codes, IndexError in divide during wrap). The statement itself is a title plus the issue URL.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed (v4, v6, v7, v8 all kaggle_env_pass=false), each with the same hidden-test IndexError in divide(). None of them stripped control codes; each invented a different cause. v4 made `tokens` Optional and returned early on None. v7 added the same None early-return plus a stray test_append_tokens.py at the repo root. v8 skipped tokens whose content is None. v6 deleted `self._length = offset`, which has nothing to do with the bug. None of them reproduced the crash through Console.print with wrapping, and none compared the method with Text.append, which calls strip_control_codes.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only 'Fixed exception in <func>' plus an issue link you cannot read, do not guess a None guard. Diff <func> against its sibling methods in the same class (for example append vs append_tokens, or __init__ vs a from_* constructor) and look for a normalisation or sanitisation call the siblings make and <func> skips. Then reproduce with awkward but realistic inputs (control characters such as \r, \b and \x1b, tabs, newlines, unicode) pushed through the real consumer path (render, wrap, serialise), not by calling the function on its own. A fix that only adds a None or type check almost never matches an upstream 'exception' PR.
